title: Before you read a word, know who sent it.
subtitle: The sender sets the weight of the message

row.title: the Book
sub: truth with no doubt in it

then: Makkah, a city full of hostility toward the new message. The surah opens by naming its source: {idea}the Almighty, the All-Wise.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ used to recite this surah every night.
now: You scroll past a hundred messages a day. Most you skim. Then one comes from your mother, or a doctor with your results, and you read every word twice. {idea}Who sent it changes how you read it.{/idea}
old: The Quran is a book I should get around to reading properly.
new: It is sent down by the Almighty and the Wise, so every line deserves my full attention.
try: Before you open the Quran today, pause for three breaths and remember who it is from.

title: The Book came with truth, so give Him a pure heart.
subtitle: Sincerity is the first reply to revelation

row.title: mixed motives
sub: for Him, and to be seen

then: The command is to the Prophet ﷺ first: worship Allah alone, and teach people that {idea}no one and nothing shares that right.{/idea} The message landed among people who prayed to many.
now: You post a photo of the charity drive. You mention the night prayer in passing. Small things, but they pull the deed toward the audience. {trap}Half for Him, half for the likes.{/trap} The verse asks for one address only.
old: As long as I do good things, why I do them matters less.
new: The truth of the Book asks for a deed done for Allah alone.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will ever know about.

title: No go-between is needed to come near Him.
subtitle: The excuse of the middlemen

row.title: the pure religion
sub: accepted only if sincere to Him

then: The idolaters said: {trap}we only worship them so they bring us near to Allah.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they pictured Allah like their kings, reached through ministers. But even the angels intercede only by His leave.
now: You think you need the right connection for everything: the cousin at the bank, the friend in HR. Then you carry that habit into your prayer, as if Allah only listens through someone else. {idea}He hears you directly.{/idea}
old: I am too far from Allah to ask Him myself.
new: Nearness to Him comes through sincere worship, not through a middleman.
try: Make one dua today in your own words, straight to Him, about something you have been hesitant to ask.

title: He is One, and needs no son beside Him.
subtitle: Why the claim of offspring falls apart
then: Some in Makkah claimed the angels were Allah's daughters. Ibn Kathir explains the verse as a condition that shows how empty the claim is: {idea}it is impossible, and He is far above it.{/idea}
now: You picture Allah the way you picture people: tired, needing help, needing someone to carry on. Without noticing, you shrink Him to your size. {idea}The One, the Irresistible{/idea} does not fit that picture.
old: I imagine Allah a bit like a powerful person, only bigger.
new: He is One and Irresistible, with no need for anyone at all.
try: Say subhanallah slowly ten times today, meaning: You are above every limit I picture.

title: Night wraps day, day wraps night, and He still forgives.
subtitle: Might that runs the sky and forgives you
then: Ibn Kathir says night and day chase each other without stopping, and the sun and moon run until a term {idea}known to Allah{/idea}, ending on the Day of Resurrection. Then, beside His might, He is {reward}Oft-Forgiving to those who turn back.{/reward}
now: You watch the sunset from the bus window on the way home, tired, thinking about what you got wrong today. The same hand turning that sky is waiting for you to turn back. {reward}Big enough to run the sky, close enough to forgive you.{/reward}
old: Someone that powerful has no time for my small mistakes.
new: The One who runs the sun and moon is also the One who keeps forgiving.
try: At sunset today, watch the sky change for one minute and ask Him for forgiveness.

title: He shaped you in three darknesses. How can you turn away?
subtitle: Your own beginning as the argument

row.title: Such is Allah your Lord
sub: so how are you turned away?

then: Ibn Kathir lists the stages: a drop, a clot, a lump, then bones and flesh, then the soul. The three darknesses are womb, placenta, and belly. {idea}The One who did all that is your Lord.{/idea}
now: You sit in a hospital corridor waiting for an ultrasound, staring at a grainy screen. A heartbeat you did not build, in a darkness no one could reach. {idea}That was you once too.{/idea}
old: I built my life with my own hands.
new: I was formed in darkness before I could do anything, so my Lord is the One who formed me.
try: Thank Allah today for one part of your body you have never once thought about.

title: He needs nothing from you, yet loves your gratitude.
subtitle: Thankfulness is for your own good

row.title: your own load
sub: no one carries it for you

then: Ibn Kathir cites the words of Musa: if all on earth disbelieve, Allah is still Rich. {idea}Gratitude pleases Him and He increases His favor.{/idea} And each person answers only for their own deeds.
now: Payday. You check the balance, pay the bills, and move on. The verse does not ask for a speech, just a thankful heart. {reward}He likes it for you, not for Himself.{/reward} And on the Day, your friends cannot carry your account.
old: My worship is something I give to Allah.
new: Allah needs nothing; my gratitude is a gift that comes back to me.
try: Write down three things you are thankful for tonight, and say alhamdulillah for each one.

title: Desperate in the storm, forgetful in the calm.
subtitle: The prayer we drop once the trouble passes
then: Ibn Kathir explains that in need a person calls on Allah alone, but {trap}once relieved, forgets the prayer{/trap} and sets up rivals. The warning, enjoy your disbelief a little, is a stern one.
now: The night before the exam results, you prayed like never before. The scan came back clear and you promised to change. Three weeks later the prayer mat is folded away. {idea}The calm is where the test really starts.{/idea}
old: I turn to Allah when I really need Him.
new: Turning to Him in hardship is easy; staying with Him after relief is the proof.
try: Think of one prayer Allah answered for you. Thank Him for it today, by name.

title: Standing at night, between fear and hope.
subtitle: Those who know are not like those who do not
then: After the forgetful one of the last verse comes the one who prays in the depths of the night, {idea}with both fear and hope.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes the Prophet ﷺ said when both meet in a dying heart, Allah gives what it hopes for.
now: Two in the morning. Everyone is asleep, the phone is face down. You stand for two short rakahs, not sure if you are doing it right. {reward}Afraid and hopeful at once.{/reward} That mix is what knowing looks like.
old: Either I am scared of Allah or I am at peace with Him.
new: Real knowledge holds fear and hope together, like two wings.
try: Set an alarm ten minutes before Fajr tonight and pray two rakahs before it.

title: Allah's earth is wide, and patience is paid beyond measure.
subtitle: When a place gets too narrow for your faith
then: The surah introduction says this was sent before the migration to Abyssinia, and some reports link it to Jafar ibn Abi Talib and his companions. {idea}Allah's earth is spacious.{/idea} Al-Awzai said the patient's reward {reward}will not be weighed or measured.{/reward}
now: The office where everyone mocks your prayer breaks. The friend group that pulls you somewhere you do not want to go. You feel trapped. {idea}The earth is wider than one room.{/idea} And every quiet day of patience is being counted without a ceiling.
old: I am stuck here and nothing can change.
new: Allah's earth is wide, and the patience I show where I am is rewarded without limit.
try: Name one place that keeps squeezing your faith, and take one small step toward a better space.

title: The Messenger says it first about himself.
subtitle: The teacher is under the same order

row.title: the same order
sub: he says it of himself first

then: Ibn Kathir explains the meaning: {idea}I am commanded to worship Allah alone in all sincerity, with no partner.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ is told to announce it as his own duty before calling others to it.
now: You tell your little brother to put his phone down at dinner, with yours glowing in your lap. You give advice in the family group chat that you skip yourself. {idea}Start with I am commanded.{/idea}
old: I know what others should be doing.
new: The first person the message is for is me.
try: Pick one piece of advice you often give others and follow it yourself today.

title: Be the first to submit, not the last to follow.
subtitle: Leading by going first
then: In Makkah almost no one around him had accepted. Still, the command was to be {idea}the first of the Muslims{/idea}, submitting before anyone else, whether others came or not.
now: Your family has always prayed late. Your team always cuts the same corner. You wait for someone else to change first so you will not stand out. {reward}Someone has to be first.{/reward}
old: I will start once the people around me start.
new: Submission does not wait for a crowd; I can be the first.
try: Be the first in your home to pray the next prayer on time, without saying anything.

title: Even the Messenger said: I fear that Day.
subtitle: If he fears it, how should I feel
then: Ibn Kathir explains this is a conditional sentence. {idea}If it is said by the Prophet ﷺ, it applies even more to everyone else.{/idea} The great Day is the Day of Resurrection.
now: You tell yourself you are fine. You do not drink, you do not steal, you mostly pray. Then you remember the one sent to teach us said this. {idea}Healthy fear keeps you awake, not anxious.{/idea}
old: I am a decent person, so the Day is not my worry.
new: If the Prophet ﷺ said he fears that Day, I should take my own conduct seriously.
try: Before sleeping, think of one thing you did today you would want to fix, and ask forgiveness for it.

title: Allah alone I worship. Say it plainly.
subtitle: A clear line under pressure
then: The surah introduction says the Prophet ﷺ was told to tell them plainly that persecution would not turn him from his way. {idea}Allah alone I worship, sincere to Him in my religion.{/idea}
now: At the work dinner someone jokes about your fasting. You laugh along and change the subject. No need to argue, but no need to hide. {idea}This is who I worship.{/idea}
old: I keep my faith quiet so no one makes it awkward.
new: I can say calmly and clearly who I worship, without needing approval.
try: Next time someone asks about your faith, answer simply and kindly instead of changing the topic.

title: The real loss is losing yourself and your family.
subtitle: What counts as losing, on the Day
then: Worship what you like, the verse says, as a warning and a disowning. Ibn Kathir explains the losers are {trap}separated from their families and will never meet again.{/trap} That is the clearest loss.
now: You lose a deal and cannot sleep. You lose a promotion and sulk for a week. Meanwhile the dinners with your kids get shorter and the prayers slip. {idea}Ask what you are really afraid of losing.{/idea}
old: Losing means missing out on money or position.
new: The loss that matters is losing myself and the people I love on the Day.
try: Put your phone away during one family meal today and talk with them properly.

title: He warns you now so you never have to face it.
subtitle: A warning given out of care
then: After naming the loss of self and family, the verse describes the Fire in one line. Ibn Kathir says Allah tells us this {idea}so that His servants keep away from sin.{/idea} It ends tenderly: O My servants.
now: A parent grabs a child's hand at the edge of a busy road and shouts. It sounds harsh, but it is love. {idea}The warning comes first so the harm never does.{/idea} And notice He still calls you His.
old: Verses about the Fire are only meant to scare me.
new: He warns because He wants me safe, and He still calls me His servant.
try: Think of one habit you know is harmful, and take one step away from it today.

title: Good news for those who walked away from false gods.
subtitle: Turning away and turning back
then: Ibn Kathir reports it was said to be about Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr and Salman al-Farisi, men who {idea}left idol worship and searched for the truth.{/idea} The correct view, he says, is that it covers everyone like them.
now: You quit the thing that was ruling your evenings: the game, the feed, the late nights. But an empty hour fills up again fast. {idea}Leaving is half. Turning to Him is the other half.{/idea}
old: Giving up a bad thing is enough.
new: The good news is for those who leave false masters and also turn back to Allah.
try: Take one hour you used to spend on a habit you dropped, and give ten minutes of it to Allah.

title: Listen to everything, follow the best of it.
subtitle: How guided people listen
then: Ibn Kathir says these are the ones who {idea}understand the Word and act on it{/idea}, like Musa told to take the Tawrah firmly and have his people take the best in it.
now: You finish a talk on your commute and think: that was good. By lunch you cannot remember one point. {idea}Pick the best line and live it today.{/idea}
old: Hearing a good reminder is the same as benefiting from it.
new: Guidance is listening closely and then following the best of what I heard.
try: From the next reminder you hear, pick one line and act on it before the day ends.

title: You cannot save someone; only Allah guides.
subtitle: The limit of what you can do for others
then: The question is put to the Prophet ﷺ himself: can you rescue one who is in the Fire? Ibn Kathir explains {idea}no one can guide him apart from Allah.{/idea} The Prophet's ﷺ task was to convey.
now: Your brother has stopped praying. You have tried every argument, sent every video. You lie awake feeling it is your failure. {idea}Keep caring, keep praying for him, and put the weight down.{/idea}
old: If someone I love goes astray, I have failed.
new: My job is to care and convey; guiding hearts belongs to Allah alone.
try: Make dua tonight, by name, for one person you have been trying to change.

title: Rooms built above rooms, with rivers below.
subtitle: A promise Allah does not break
then: Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ said there are rooms in Paradise seen from inside and out, and when asked who they are for, said: {reward}those who speak kindly, feed others, and pray at night while people sleep.{/reward}
now: You save for years for a small flat, checking listings every night. The verse points to a home that no inflation touches. {reward}And the price is kind words, a shared meal, and a quiet prayer.{/reward}
old: Paradise feels too far away to think about.
new: It is a promise Allah never breaks, built by ordinary kindness and night prayer.
try: Feed someone today: a neighbor, a coworker, or a stranger, even with something small.

title: Green, then yellow, then dust. So is this life.
subtitle: The life of a crop as a mirror
then: Ibn Kathir says this is a reminder that {idea}this world is green and fresh, then it grows old.{/idea} The young man becomes old and weak, then death comes. The blessed one is whose state after death is good.
now: You scroll back through photos from ten years ago. The face, the energy, the friends who were always around. {idea}The field always turns yellow.{/idea} The question is what you planted while it was green.
old: I have plenty of time; I am still young.
new: Every green season turns, so I should invest in what lasts beyond it.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself today and ask: what good did I do since then?

title: An open chest with light, or a heart gone hard.
subtitle: Two hearts hearing the same remembrance

key.label: The sign of a hard heart

then: Right after the image of a field drying out, the verse turns to hearts. Ibn Kathir says the hard-hearted {trap}do not become soft when Allah is mentioned.{/trap} The open heart {reward}is on light from its Lord.{/reward}
now: The imam recites a verse that once made you cry. Now you are checking the time. Nothing moves. {idea}A heart can dry out like a field, and it can be watered again.{/idea}
old: Feeling nothing in prayer is just how it is now.
new: A heart that stops softening is a warning sign, and Allah can open it again.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to soften your heart.

title: Skin shivers, then the heart settles.
subtitle: How the best speech moves those who fear Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Quran pairs things: believers then disbelievers, Paradise then Hell. So {trap}the warnings make skin shiver{/trap}, then {reward}hope softens the heart.{/reward} Qatadah said they wept quietly; they did not lose their minds.
now: Late at night you play a recitation with headphones. One verse makes the hair on your arm rise. A few verses later you feel calm. {idea}Fear, then hope. That is the Book working.{/idea}
old: Being moved by the Quran means big emotion.
new: The real sign is a quiet shiver of fear and then a heart at rest.
try: Listen to one page of Quran with a translation tonight, slowly, and notice where you feel it.

title: Nothing left to shield him but his own face.
subtitle: Not equal to the one who comes safe
then: After the soft hearts of the last verse comes the other side. Ibn Kathir says the wrongdoer is rebuked: {trap}taste what you used to earn.{/trap} Is he like the one who comes secure on the Day? The answer is left to you.
now: Every small cruelty, every lie that saved you trouble, every unkind word goes into a ledger you never see. {idea}What comes back is what you sent ahead.{/idea} And you can still change what you send.
old: What happens to me after death is out of my hands.
new: What I meet on the Day is what I earned, so I can start earning safety now.
try: Undo one small wrong today: an apology, a returned item, a corrected word.

title: It came from where they never looked.
subtitle: The danger of feeling safe
then: Ibn Kathir says earlier generations who denied their Messengers {trap}were destroyed for their sins, and none could protect them.{/trap} The Quraysh were being reminded that the same could reach them.
now: You keep saying you will fix it later: the prayer, the debt, the relative you stopped talking to. You assume you will get a warning first. {idea}Later is not promised to arrive with notice.{/idea}
old: I will sort things out when I see the end coming.
new: It often comes from where no one looks, so the time to set things right is now.
try: Pick one thing you keep postponing with Allah or a person, and do the first step today.

title: Disgrace here was small next to what comes after.
subtitle: If they only knew
then: Ibn Kathir says the earlier deniers tasted disgrace in this life, and {trap}what is promised in the Hereafter is worse.{/trap} So those addressed, who rejected the Seal of the Prophets ﷺ, should beware.
now: You are terrified of being embarrassed: caught out at work, exposed in the group chat. You will do almost anything to avoid that shame. {idea}Fear the account that lasts more than the one that fades.{/idea}
old: Public shame is the worst thing that could happen to me.
new: Worldly disgrace passes; what I face before Allah is what really matters.
try: Tonight, ask yourself which you worry about more: people's opinion or Allah's. Be honest.

title: Every kind of example, so you will remember.
subtitle: Why the Quran teaches in pictures
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah explains things {idea}by setting forth examples and parables, because they bring the meaning closer to people's minds.{/idea} Some are drawn from people's own lives.
now: You forget the lecture but remember the teacher's story about the broken vase. Pictures stick. {idea}The Quran's examples are made to stick.{/idea} When you meet one, ask where you are in it.
old: The parables in the Quran are about other people.
new: Each example is set out so I can see myself and remember.
try: Next time you read a parable in the Quran, write one line on where you see yourself in it.

title: Plain words with no crookedness in them.
subtitle: A clear Book, so you can be mindful

row.title: taqwa
sub: heed the warning, seek the promise

then: Ibn Kathir explains it is {idea}in a plain Arabic tongue, with no crookedness, deviation or confusion.{/idea} It was revealed this way so people would heed its warnings and strive for its promises.
now: You keep the Quran on a high shelf, thinking it is too deep for you. Then you read a single page with a translation and find it speaking directly. {idea}It was built to be understood.{/idea}
old: The Quran is too complex for someone like me.
new: It was sent plain and straight so that I could understand it and be mindful.
try: Read one short surah with its translation today, start to finish.

title: Many quarreling masters, or one Master.
subtitle: The exhausted servant and the settled one
then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said this is {idea}the parable of the idolater and the sincere believer.{/idea} One slave is fought over by partners; the other belongs to one man. Ibn Kathir says the answer is so clear the verse ends with praise.
now: Your boss wants one thing, your in-laws another, your followers a third, your own ego a fourth. You are worn out trying to please them all. {trap}Many masters.{/trap} {reward}Serve One, and the rest fall into place.{/reward}
old: I have to keep everyone happy.
new: Belonging to Allah alone frees me from being torn between many masters.
try: Next decision you face today, ask only: what would please Allah here?

title: You will die, and they will die too.
subtitle: The one appointment no one misses
then: Ibn Kathir notes this is one of the verses {idea}Abu Bakr recited when the Prophet ﷺ died{/idea}, so people would accept that he had truly passed. Even the best of creation would taste death.
now: You argue with a relative for years over an inheritance, a slight, a wedding seating plan. Both of you act as if there is all the time in the world. {idea}You will die. They will die.{/idea} Then what was it all for?
old: Death is something that happens to other people, later.
new: Death came even to the Prophet ﷺ, so I should live each day as if I will stand before Allah.
try: Think of one quarrel you are holding onto, and ask if it would matter at your funeral.

title: Every unsettled dispute will be reopened before your Lord.
subtitle: Arguments do not end at the grave
then: When this was revealed, Az-Zubayr asked if their wrongs against others would be repeated. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}yes, until everyone gets their right back.{/idea} Az-Zubayr said: by Allah, this is a very serious matter.
now: The money you borrowed and never mentioned again. The coworker whose credit you took. The harsh words to your mother. {trap}They are not closed.{/trap} {reward}You can settle them here, while it is still easy.{/reward}
old: Old wrongs fade if nobody brings them up.
new: Every right will be restored before Allah, so I should return what I owe now.
try: Settle one small debt or wrong today: pay it back, give credit, or apologize.

title: Lying about Allah and rejecting truth: the double wrong.
subtitle: Who could be more unjust
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolaters claimed Allah had partners and daughters, then rejected the truth brought by the Messengers. {trap}They combined both falsehoods{/trap}, which is why no one does more wrong.
now: Someone shows you clear proof you were wrong. You feel the sting, and the easy move is to twist the facts and dismiss them. {idea}The test is what you do when truth reaches you.{/idea}
old: If I don't like what the truth says, I can just ignore it.
new: Rejecting truth once it reaches me is among the greatest wrongs.
try: Think of one point someone made that you brushed off. Reconsider it honestly today.

title: The one who brought the truth, and those who believed it.
subtitle: Bringing truth and accepting it

key.label: The contrast with the last verse

then: Mujahid and others said the one who brought the truth is {idea}the Messenger ﷺ{/idea}, and those who believed in it are the Muslims. Ibn Abbas said they are the ones who {idea}fear and shun shirk.{/idea}
now: Someone says something true at the family dinner and the table goes quiet. You know they are right. You can stay silent, or be the one who says: yes, that is true. {reward}Confirming truth is its own good deed.{/reward}
old: Only the one who speaks up first gets credit.
new: Believing and backing the truth when it comes is also taqwa.
try: Next time someone says something true and unpopular, quietly back them up.

title: Whatever they wish for, with their Lord.
subtitle: The reward of the doers of good
then: Ibn Kathir explains it is in Paradise: {reward}whatever they ask for, they will have.{/reward} It is called the reward of the muhsinin, those who do good.
now: Your wish list grows every month: a better car, a bigger place, a holiday. Every wish met makes room for a new one. {reward}There is a place where wanting finally rests.{/reward}
old: I will be happy once I get the next thing I want.
new: The wishes that are fully met are kept with my Lord for those who do good.
try: Delete one item from your shopping cart today and give its price, or part of it, in charity.

title: Your worst erased, your best becomes the measure.
subtitle: How Allah rewards the doers of good
then: Ibn Kathir links it to the verse about people whose {reward}best deeds are accepted and whose evil deeds are overlooked.{/reward} This is the reward for those who brought and confirmed the truth.
now: You keep replaying the worst thing you ever did, the night you would undo if you could. It feels like the headline of your life. {reward}For those who turn to Him and do good, the worst is erased and the best is the measure.{/reward}
old: My worst mistake is who I really am.
new: Allah can wipe my worst and pay me by the measure of my best.
try: Do one good deed today with full effort, the kind you would want to be measured by.

title: Is Allah not enough for His servant?
subtitle: When they try to frighten you

row.title: the idols
sub: used to scare the Prophet ﷺ

row.title: Allah suffices
sub: for the one who relies on Him

then: Ibn Kathir says the idolaters {trap}tried to scare the Messenger ﷺ with their idols.{/trap} The reply is a question: {idea}is Allah not sufficient for His servant?{/idea} Some read it as His servants, covering all who rely on Him.
now: A manager hints your contract may not be renewed. A relative warns that people will talk. Fear sits in your chest at 3am. {idea}Is Allah not enough for you?{/idea}
old: I need to cover every angle myself or I am unsafe.
new: Allah is enough for the one who worships Him and relies on Him.
try: When a fear comes up today, say hasbunallah and name the fear to Him.

title: Whom Allah guides, no one can mislead.
subtitle: Guidance that cannot be taken away

row.title: Allah guides
sub: the one who turns to Him

then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}whoever relies on Him and turns to Him will never be forsaken{/idea}, for He is the Almighty whom no one can overwhelm. This came while the Prophet ﷺ faced threats in Makkah.
now: You worry that the new job, the new city, the new friends will pull you away from your deen. You feel fragile. {reward}Stay turned toward Him{/reward}, and no crowd can pull out what He placed.
old: My faith could be taken from me at any time by the wrong people.
new: When I keep turning to Allah, no one can mislead what He guides.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to keep your heart firm on His way.

title: No one can lift His harm or hold back His mercy.
subtitle: Sufficient for me is Allah
then: The idolaters admitted Allah created the heavens and earth, yet called on others. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet's ﷺ words: {idea}if the whole nation gathered to harm you, they could not, except what Allah decreed.{/idea}
now: You keep checking the job portal, refreshing the inbox, calling the friend with connections. {trap}As if they decide.{/trap} Do your part, then rest: {reward}if He wills mercy, no one can block it.{/reward}
old: My outcome depends on the right people saying yes.
new: No one can stop a mercy Allah sends, so I rely on Him and do my part.
try: After doing all you can for one worry today, say hasbiyallahu alayhi tawakkaltu and let it go.

title: Do your work, I will do mine. You will see.
subtitle: Staying on your way under pressure
then: Ibn Kathir calls it {trap}a threat and a warning{/trap} to those who opposed. The surah introduction says the Prophet ﷺ was to tell them their persecution would never deter him; {idea}he would continue his mission.{/idea}
now: Your friends mock your choice not to drink at the office party. You could argue all night. Or you smile, drink your juice, and keep living your way. {idea}Time shows whose way was wise.{/idea}
old: I need to convince everyone that I am right.
new: I keep doing what is right and leave the outcome to show itself.
try: Next time your faith is mocked, do not argue. Stay kind and stay the course.

title: Disgrace here, and a lasting punishment after.
subtitle: The end the warning points to
then: Ibn Kathir says the disgracing torment comes {trap}in this world{/trap} and the enduring one on the Day of Resurrection. He ends: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from that.{/idea}
now: You read a warning like this and quickly think of someone else who deserves it. {idea}Turn it inward.{/idea} Which part of my own way of living would I not want to bring before Him?
old: Warnings like this are for the really bad people.
new: Every warning is a chance for me to seek refuge and fix my own path.
try: Say a'udhu billah sincerely once today and mean it for yourself.

title: Guidance benefits you; straying harms only you.
subtitle: The messenger is not a guard over people
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Book is for all of creation, and {idea}the benefit of guidance returns to the one guided.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was told he is not responsible for guiding them; his duty is to convey.
now: You pray, you fast, you give, and part of you thinks you are doing Allah a favor. Or you skip it all and think it only affects your mood. {idea}It all comes back to you.{/idea}
old: My worship is something I do for Allah's sake only, as a favor.
new: Every step of guidance benefits my own soul, and every step away harms it.
try: Before your next prayer, tell yourself: this is for my own soul.

title: Every night He takes your soul, and most mornings returns it.
subtitle: Sleep as a small death

row.title: a return
sub: my soul sent back to me

then: Ibn Kathir describes sleep as a lesser death. The Prophet ﷺ taught a bedtime dua: {idea}if You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it.{/idea}
now: You fall asleep scrolling, phone on your face. You wake to an alarm and reach for it again. {reward}Your soul was taken and handed back.{/reward} That deserves more than a groan.
old: Waking up every day is just normal.
new: Every waking is my soul returned to me, a new term granted by Allah.
try: Tonight, before sleep, say: In Your name, my Lord, I lie down, and in Your name I rise.

title: Intercessors that own nothing and understand nothing.
subtitle: Whom do you rely on to speak for you
then: Ibn Kathir says they took idols {trap}on the basis of their own whims, with no evidence.{/trap} These cannot think, hear, or see, yet they were expected to plead before Allah.
now: You carry a lucky charm to the interview. You trust your family name to get you through. You think your title will speak for you someday. {idea}Ask what it actually owns.{/idea}
old: Something or someone will put in a good word for me.
new: Things that own nothing cannot speak for me before Allah.
try: Notice one object or habit you treat as a good-luck guarantee, and let it go today.

title: All intercession belongs to Allah alone.
subtitle: No one speaks without His permission

row.title: by His leave
sub: for whom He is pleased with

then: Ibn Kathir explains that intercession {idea}avails only for one Allah is pleased with, by His permission.{/idea} He cites the Throne Verse: who can intercede with Him except by His leave?
now: You hope that being near pious people will be enough: the right mosque, the right circle, the scholar friend. Good company helps. {idea}But the one to please is Allah Himself.{/idea}
old: Being close to good people will cover me.
new: All intercession is His to grant, so my effort goes to pleasing Him.
try: Do one act today purely to please Allah, not to be seen near anyone.

title: Mention Allah alone and some hearts recoil.
subtitle: What your heart does at His name
then: Ibn Kathir says when it was said there is no god but Allah alone, {trap}their hearts recoiled in horror{/trap}, as Mujahid put it. Hearts that could not accept good accepted evil instead. At the mention of their idols, they rejoiced.
now: Someone mentions your favorite player and you light up for twenty minutes. Someone mentions Allah at the same table and you feel a little awkward. {idea}Notice what makes your heart brighten.{/idea}
old: How I feel when Allah is mentioned does not say much about me.
new: What my heart rejoices at shows what it truly loves.
try: Bring up something you love about Allah in one conversation today, and notice how it feels.

title: When arguments go nowhere, take them to the Judge.
subtitle: A dua for when people disagree
then: After the idolaters' aversion to Tawhid, the Prophet ﷺ is taught to call on Allah. Aishah reported he opened his night prayer with these words, asking: {idea}guide me to the truth in what they differ over.{/idea}
now: The family group chat is at war again over something religious. Everyone is sure. You are tired. {idea}Step out of the argument and into this dua.{/idea} Ask to be guided to the truth yourself.
old: I have to win this argument or the truth will lose.
new: Allah will judge between us; my part is to ask Him to guide me to the truth.
try: Before your night prayer, ask Allah to guide you to the truth in one matter people dispute.

title: The whole earth twice over would not buy a way out.
subtitle: What they never reckoned with
then: Ibn Kathir says no ransom will be accepted, {trap}even an earth full of gold.{/trap} Then {idea}there will appear to them from Allah what they never reckoned{/idea}, a reality they never imagined.
now: You work extra shifts to build a buffer: savings, insurance, a second property. Good planning for this life. {idea}But nothing in the bank pays for the next one.{/idea} Only what you did with it.
old: Enough money can solve almost any problem.
new: Not even the whole earth twice over could buy safety on that Day.
try: Spend one small amount today purely for Allah, as an investment that actually crosses.

title: What they laughed at closed in around them.
subtitle: When mockery comes back

row.title: it returns
sub: what you mock can surround you

then: Ibn Kathir explains they will see the result of the sins they committed, and {trap}the punishment they used to make fun of will surround them.{/trap} The warning is aimed at those who laughed it off.
now: A clip mocking religious people goes round your friends and you send the laughing emoji. It is easy to laugh at what you do not take seriously. {idea}Be careful what you treat as a joke.{/idea}
old: Joking about serious things is harmless.
new: What I mock today may be exactly what I have to face later.
try: Skip one joke today that makes light of faith, even if everyone else laughs.

title: I earned this myself. No, it is a test.
subtitle: The danger of crediting yourself
then: The same pattern as verse 8, now with a new claim. Ibn Kathir says the man thinks {trap}Allah gave it because I deserve it.{/trap} Allah replies: {idea}it is a trial, to see if he will obey.{/idea} Qarun said the same.
now: The promotion comes through after months of praying. Two weeks later you are telling people it was your skills and strategy. {idea}Skills are real. So is the test.{/idea}
old: I got this because of my own talent and hard work.
new: Every blessing is a test of what I will do with it.
try: Think of your latest success and say out loud: this is from Allah, to test me.

title: The same boast was made before, and it saved no one.
subtitle: An old claim with an old ending
then: Ibn Kathir explains that earlier nations {trap}made the same claims, and all they had gathered did not save them.{/trap} Qarun was told others stronger than him had been destroyed before.
now: You read about the tycoon who said he built it all alone, and then lost it in a year. Every generation has someone who says it. {idea}The line is old, and so is how it ends.{/idea}
old: What I build will protect me.
new: Many before me said the same, and what they earned did not save them.
try: Read the story of Qarun in Surah Al-Qasas this week, slowly.

title: What they earned caught up with them. No one outruns it.
subtitle: Consequences come home
then: Ibn Kathir says those addressed would be overtaken by {trap}the evil results of what they earned, just as happened to earlier peoples{/trap}, and they will never be able to escape.
now: The shortcut on the expense report. The rumor you started at school. You moved on, but deeds have a way of coming home. {idea}Better to meet them with repentance than to be overtaken.{/idea}
old: If I got away with it then, it is over.
new: What I earn follows me, so I should turn back before it overtakes me.
try: Fix one quiet wrong today before it has a chance to catch up with you.

title: More or less, provision is His to give.
subtitle: Wealth is not a verdict on you
then: Ending the passage on the boastful man, Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}gives plenty to some and restricts it for others.{/idea} Wealth is not proof of merit. In this is a lesson for those who believe.
now: Your cousin's salary is triple yours and the family treats him like the success story. You feel small at every wedding. {idea}Provision is distributed by Allah, not earned like a rank.{/idea}
old: Having more money means I am doing better in every way.
new: Allah widens and narrows provision as He wills; it is a test, not a grade.
try: Stop comparing your income to one person today, and thank Allah for what you have.

title: Do not despair. He forgives all sins.
subtitle: The door that is always open
then: Ibn Abbas reported that people who had done terrible things asked the Prophet ﷺ if there was expiation, and this came down. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah forgives all sins of those who repent, even if they are like the foam of the sea.{/reward}
now: It is three in the morning and you are sure you have used up your chances. The same sin, again. You stop even asking. {reward}He still calls you My servants.{/reward} {idea}Despair is the trap, not the sin.{/idea}
old: I have done too much for Allah to forgive me.
new: No sin is bigger than His mercy for someone who turns back.
try: Tonight, ask Allah's forgiveness for the sin you feel most ashamed of, and do not give up asking.

title: Turn back and submit, before help runs out.
subtitle: Hope with a deadline
then: Right after the promise not to despair comes the condition. Ibn Kathir says forgiveness of all sins is {idea}for the one who repents{/idea}, and here the call is to turn back {trap}before the punishment comes and no help is given.{/trap}
now: The last verse made you breathe again. Now the next one says: do not wait. You plan to get serious after the wedding, after the exams, after the move. {idea}The door is open today.{/idea}
old: Allah is merciful, so I can repent whenever I am ready.
new: His mercy is wide, and the time to turn back is now.
try: Choose one sin you plan to quit someday, and make today day one.

title: Follow the best of what was sent, before it comes suddenly.
subtitle: No warning bell rings first
then: The call continues: after turning back and submitting, {idea}follow the best of what your Lord sent down{/idea}, before the punishment comes {trap}suddenly, while you do not perceive.{/trap}
now: A colleague, healthy at forty, does not come back from the weekend. Everyone is in shock. Nobody got a reminder notification. {idea}Act on the best you know while you can.{/idea}
old: I will know when it is time to get serious.
new: It can come without warning, so I follow the best of the guidance today.
try: Pick the one good thing you keep meaning to start, and start it today.

title: So you will never have to say: oh, my regret.
subtitle: The first sentence of regret
then: The calls to return in verses 53 to 55 are given {idea}lest a soul should say{/idea} this sentence. Allah shows the regret in advance so it never has to be spoken: {trap}I neglected my duty to Allah, and I mocked.{/trap}
now: You can picture saying it about a parent you never called back: I wish I had. The verse lets you hear that sentence now, about Allah, {idea}while you can still change the ending.{/idea}
old: Regret is something to deal with if it ever comes.
new: Allah lets me hear the words of regret now so I never have to say them.
try: Write one sentence you would regret not having done for Allah, and do part of it this week.

title: If only Allah had guided me: the excuse that fails.
subtitle: Blaming guidance you were given
then: The second thing a regretful soul might say. The guidance was in front of them all along; the call to turn back and follow the best of what was sent had just been given in the verses before. {trap}This excuse will not hold.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself you would pray more if you just felt guided, if a sign came. Meanwhile the Quran sits on your phone, unopened. {idea}The guidance is already in your pocket.{/idea}
old: I will change once Allah sends me a sign.
new: The guidance has already reached me; waiting for more is an excuse.
try: Open the Quran app today and read one page instead of waiting to feel ready.

title: If only I had one more chance. You have it now.
subtitle: The wish for another turn
then: The third thing a soul might say, now {trap}on seeing the punishment{/trap}: if only I could go back and be among those who do good. The verses before showed the door is open {idea}before that moment, not after.{/idea}
now: You wake up this morning. You breathe, you scroll, you grab coffee. Somewhere in the next world, someone is wishing for exactly this. {reward}Another turn. That is today.{/reward}
old: There will always be another chance to get it right.
new: This life is the second chance people will beg for, and I am living it.
try: Do one good deed today and tell yourself: this is the turn I would wish for.

title: But My verses did come to you.
subtitle: The answer to every excuse
then: This answers the soul who said: if only Allah had guided me. {idea}The verses had come.{/idea} The problem was never a lack of guidance; it was {trap}denial and arrogance.{/trap}
now: You know the verse about backbiting. You have heard the talk on lying at work. It is not that you do not know. {trap}Sometimes it is just not wanting to be told.{/trap}
old: I would follow the truth if only it were clearer.
new: Often the truth is clear enough; what holds me back is pride.
try: Name one thing you already know you should do, and admit to Allah that pride is in the way.

title: Lies about Allah show on the face that Day.
subtitle: Arrogance and its home
then: Ibn Kathir says they lied about Allah by claiming He had partners or offspring, so {trap}their faces will be dark because of their lies.{/trap} Their home is the result of {trap}stubborn pride and refusal to follow the truth.{/trap}
now: You catch yourself saying something about Allah you never checked: He would never forgive that person, He definitely wants this for me. {idea}Speak about Him only with knowledge, and humbly.{/idea}
old: Speaking loosely about what Allah wants is harmless.
new: Saying false things about Allah is serious, and humility is the cure.
try: Before saying what Allah will or will not do today, stop and ask if you actually know.

title: No harm will touch them, and no grief.
subtitle: Safe on the day of the greatest terror
then: Next to the darkened faces, Ibn Kathir says the people of taqwa will be safe: {reward}the greater terror of that Day will not grieve them{/reward}; they will be removed from all evil and given all that is good.
now: You lie awake with a dozen worries: rent, health, a child far away. Some will pass, some will not. {reward}There is a safety coming that no worry can reach.{/reward} Taqwa is the road there.
old: Feeling safe means having nothing to worry about right now.
new: The safety that lasts belongs to the mindful, on the Day it matters most.
try: When a worry comes today, add: and on that Day, O Allah, make me among the safe.

title: Creator of everything, and in charge of everything.
subtitle: Nothing is outside His care

row.title: the big things
sub: the rest is up to me

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}the Creator, Lord, Sovereign and Controller of all things{/idea}; everything is under His dominion, power and guardianship.
now: You trust Allah with the big diagnosis but white-knuckle the parking spot, the traffic, the email reply. {idea}Trustee over all things means the small ones too.{/idea}
old: Allah handles the big matters; the details are on me.
new: He created and manages everything, even the details I fret about.
try: Hand one small daily stress to Allah today with a short dua instead of fretting.

title: He holds the keys of the heavens and the earth.
subtitle: Who opens and who closes

row.title: the one who denied His signs

then: Mujahid said maqalid means keys; As-Suddi said treasures. Ibn Kathir says {idea}both mean that control of all things is in Allah's hand.{/idea} Those who deny His signs are the losers.
now: You stand outside a closed door: a visa, a job offer, a rishta that went quiet. You keep knocking on people. {idea}The keys are with Him.{/idea}
old: The right person holds the key to what I need.
new: Every key to every door belongs to Allah.
try: For one closed door in your life, ask Allah directly today before asking anyone else.

title: You want me to worship something else? No.
subtitle: Refusing a compromise on worship
then: Ibn Abbas reported the idolaters invited the Messenger ﷺ {trap}to worship their gods, and they would then worship his God with him.{/trap} This verse is the reply.
now: Your friends say: come to this one thing, then we will come to the mosque with you. It sounds fair. {idea}Some things are not up for trade.{/idea} Be kind, but be clear.
old: A little compromise in faith keeps the peace.
new: Worship belongs to Allah alone and is not something to bargain with.
try: Decide in advance on one line you will not cross, so you can say no kindly when asked.

title: Shirk would wipe out every deed, even a prophet's.
subtitle: The one thing that empties the account
then: Revealed with the reply to the idolaters' offer. Ibn Kathir compares it to the verse about the prophets: {trap}had they associated others with Allah, all they did would have been of no benefit.{/trap}
now: Years of prayers, charity, fasting. Then a quiet reliance on a charm, a fortune-teller, a person you treat as all-powerful. {idea}Keep the foundation clean, or the house has nothing to stand on.{/idea}
old: With enough good deeds, a little shirk does not matter.
new: Deeds stand on pure worship; associating partners empties them.
try: Check one habit today for hidden reliance on something besides Allah, and drop it.

title: Instead: worship Allah and be grateful.
subtitle: The positive command after the warning
then: After the warning, the command. Ibn Kathir says {idea}you and those who follow you should make your worship sincerely for Allah alone{/idea}, and be among the grateful.
now: You spend energy on what you should not do. This verse shifts the focus: {idea}worship Him and be thankful.{/idea} Gratitude is the daily shape of sincere worship.
old: Faith is mostly a list of things to avoid.
new: Faith is worshipping Allah alone and living gratefully.
try: After each prayer today, name one thing you are grateful for before you get up.

title: They never measured Allah as He deserves.
subtitle: The whole earth in His grip on the Day
then: Ibn Abbas said whoever believes {idea}Allah is able to do all things{/idea} has estimated Him rightly. Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ recited this on the minbar, saying Allah will declare: {idea}I am the King.{/idea}
now: Your boss's mood decides your week. A government office decides your year. They feel huge. {idea}On that Day He will ask: where are the kings of the earth?{/idea} Measure Him rightly, and the rest shrinks.
old: The powerful people around me are what really decide things.
new: The whole earth is in Allah's grip; nothing is bigger than Him.
try: When someone powerful intimidates you today, quietly say Allahu akbar and remember who is King.

title: One blast and all fall. Another, and all stand.
subtitle: The Horn that ends and begins

row.title: the Horn
sub: all in heavens and earth fall

then: Ibn Kathir says after the blast all life ends, until only the Ever-Living remains and asks: {idea}whose is the kingdom this day?{/idea} Then the Horn is blown again and {idea}they stand, looking on.{/idea}
now: Your alarm goes off and you are up in seconds, half asleep, standing before you know it. {idea}That is how fast the second call will be.{/idea} Wake up today in a way you would like to wake up then.
old: The Day of Resurrection feels far off and unreal.
new: One call will raise everyone at once, and I will be standing among them.
try: When your alarm rings tomorrow, remember the second blast and say alhamdulillah as you rise.

title: The earth lit by its Lord's light, and the Book laid open.
subtitle: The court of the Day sets up
then: Ibn Kathir says the earth will shine when Allah comes {idea}to pass judgement.{/idea} Qatadah said the Book is the record of deeds. Ibn Abbas said the prophets will bear witness against their nations. {idea}No one will be wronged.{/idea}
now: You have watched a court case online where the evidence was missing and the guilty walked. It stung. {idea}On that Day nothing is missing and no one is wronged.{/idea} That is comfort and a warning in one.
old: Justice in this world often fails, so maybe it always does.
new: On that Day every record is laid out and judgment is in complete truth.
try: Do one thing today you would be glad to see in your own record.

title: Every soul paid in full for what it did.
subtitle: He knows best what they do
then: The verse closes the scene of judgment: {idea}every soul paid in full{/idea}, and Allah knows best what they did. Nothing depends on witnesses alone.
now: You stayed late to help a colleague and your manager never found out. You lost your temper with the cashier and no one you know saw. {idea}Both are counted, in full.{/idea}
old: If no one sees it, it does not really count.
new: Every deed, seen or unseen, is paid in full by the One who knows best.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that no one will thank you for.

title: Did no messengers come to you? Yes, they did.
subtitle: The question at the gate
then: Ibn Kathir says the keepers ask whether messengers came {idea}of your own kind, so you could have spoken to them and learned.{/idea} They answer: yes. {trap}They came and warned us, and we rejected them.{/trap}
now: Your doctor warned you. Your friend warned you. The verse you read warned you. You can picture having to say: yes, I was told. {idea}Let the answer be: yes, and I listened.{/idea}
old: Nobody ever really made the truth clear to me.
new: The warnings have reached me; what matters is whether I listen.
try: Think of one warning you have been given about your conduct, and act on it today.

title: A wretched home for the arrogant.
subtitle: Where pride leads
then: Ibn Kathir says the words are not given a speaker, as if {idea}all creation testifies they deserve it.{/idea} He names the cause: {trap}arrogance in this world and refusal to follow the truth.{/trap}
now: You notice it in small ways: refusing to say sorry first, dismissing advice from someone younger, never asking for help. {idea}Pride starts small.{/idea} So can humility.
old: A bit of pride is just self-respect.
new: Arrogance that refuses truth is what leads to the worst end.
try: Say sorry first in one disagreement today, even if you think you are partly right.

title: Peace be upon you. You have done well. Enter.
subtitle: The welcome at the open gates
then: Ibn Kathir says they go in groups, each with its peers, after injustices between them are settled. The gatekeepers meet them {reward}with greetings of peace and praise.{/reward} What follows is not mentioned, {idea}left for the heart to hope.{/idea}
now: You remember arriving home after a long trip and someone at the door saying welcome back. That warmth. {reward}Now imagine angels saying: peace be upon you, you did well.{/reward}
old: Paradise is too abstract for me to feel anything about.
new: It begins with a personal welcome: peace, you did well, come in.
try: Greet the people at home with salam today, warmly, the way you hope to be greeted.

title: Praise to Allah, who kept His promise to us.
subtitle: The first words inside
then: Inside the gates, the first words are praise. {idea}He fulfilled His promise.{/idea} They settle wherever they wish, and call it {reward}an excellent reward for those who worked.{/reward}
now: The years of waking for Fajr in winter. The money you gave when it was tight. The tongue you held. It felt like no one saw. {reward}One day you will say: He kept His promise.{/reward}
old: My small efforts for Allah probably do not add up to much.
new: Every effort is part of a promise Allah will keep in full.
try: Say alhamdulillah for one hard act of worship you kept up this year.

title: It all ends with praise to the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: The last word of the surah
then: Ibn Kathir says the praise has no named speaker, so {idea}all of creation praises Allah for His wisdom and justice.{/idea} Qatadah said Allah began creation with praise and {reward}ended it with praise.{/reward}
now: You end most days with a scroll and a sigh. Try ending it the way creation will end: {reward}alhamdulillahi rabbil alamin.{/reward} The day was judged fairly too.
old: My day ends when I run out of energy.
new: Everything ends in praise of Allah, and my day can too.
try: Before you sleep tonight, say alhamdulillahi rabbil alamin and mean it for the whole day.
